body:
Code changes: +232 -11\
Tests: +359 -1\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A simulator booted outside AO now takes taps from the Device tab and the phone again within seconds, instead of never.

- Each simulator's boot is read from the `simctl` listing AO already runs (`lastUsedAt`, which moves on every boot) and carried as `DeviceInfo.BootID`.
- Each time the device service looks at a leased device (`LiveLease`, which the Device tab and the phone poll every 2–3 s while they watch), it tells the provider which boot that device is on.
- When a running simulator turns up on a boot AO did not start, the local provider restarts the device hub once. The new hub brings fresh stream helpers; viewers reconnect on their own and stream quality is put back.
- Boots are recorded whenever the hub's helpers are known to belong to them: every simulator's when a hub starts, and the booted simulator's when AO's own boot finishes. So a reboot nobody was watching (an agent's `ao device open`, then `simctl` or Xcode reboots it) is caught on the first look afterwards, as are leases on running simulators and leases restored after a daemon restart.
- AO's own boots (`ao device open`, **Start**) already reset the helper and do not restart the hub. A failed boot leaves nothing expected behind.

## Why

The hub's per-simulator stream helper outlives the simulator's shutdown and keeps that boot's touch input. AO's boot path resets it first (`resetSimulatorHelper`, from #8893), but a simulator booted any other way (an agent's `xcrun simctl boot` or `expo run:ios`, Xcode) got the old helper back: the picture streamed and every tap went nowhere, permanently, until the hub restarted. The hub has no way to reset one simulator's helper without shutting that simulator down, so a hub restart is the only safe recovery.

## Before / After

Lab iPhone simulator held by a session, shut down and booted again with `xcrun simctl boot` while its lease was polled as a viewer does, then tapped through the hub's input socket every ~4 s. A tap counts when iOS's `backboardd` logs the touch, whatever is on screen.

| | Touches that reached iOS after the outside boot |
| --- | --- |
| Before (daemon from `main`) | 0 of 8, over 38 s |
| After | 13 of 14: the tap at 5 s landed while the hub restarted; every tap from 8 s on reached iOS |
| After, unwatched: AO booted it with nothing polling the lease, then it was rebooted with `simctl` | 9 of 10 once a viewer looked: one restart on the first look, every tap from 8 s on reached iOS |

The daemon logs `simulator booted outside AO; restarting the device hub for fresh touch input` once per outside boot. Booting the same simulator through `ao device open` restarted nothing, and the Device tab streamed normally after each restart.

## How

- `ports.DeviceBootWatcher` (optional provider interface) with `NoteBooted(DeviceInfo)`; `devices.Service.LiveLease` calls it for a running leased device.
- `local.Provider`: `bootIDs` (the boot each simulator's helper belongs to: read before the helpers are made, when a hub starts and in `Boot` before the grid start, so a reboot after the read always shows as a change; updated on each look), `ownBoots` (set by `Boot` before it boots an off simulator, cleared when `Boot` ends either way), and `restartHub`, which cancels the hub (the exit watcher does not revive a cancelled hub) and runs `EnsureReady`, falling back to `reviveHub` on failure. Only a strictly newer boot (by `lastUsedAt` time) is recorded or acted on, so a stale look cannot move the record back or restart a healthy hub. One restart at a time; a newer boot seen during one runs exactly one more after it (`runReplacements`).
- Review focus: `NoteBooted` in `adapters/device/local/provider.go`.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./internal/devices/ ./internal/adapters/device/...`, `go test ./internal/httpd/... ./internal/daemon/ ./internal/cli/`, and golangci-lint on the changed packages pass.
- New tests: an outside boot replaces the hub once (first sighting, same boot, an off device and emulators do not); AO's own boot is accepted while it runs; an unwatched AO boot followed by an outside reboot is caught on the first look; a hub start records every simulator's boot; a reboot right after `Boot` makes the helper is still caught; an older boot from a stale look is ignored; newer boots during a replacement run exactly one more; boots during a running replacement start no second one; a failed `Boot` leaves no expected boot; the listing carries `lastUsedAt` for hub-listed and `simctl`-only simulators. The provider tests fail with the fix taken out.
- Manual: the before/after run above in the device lab (macOS, iOS 26.5 simulator).

## Risks

- A restart briefly drops every device's stream (about 3–4 s), not only the rebooted one's; it happens only after a leased simulator boots outside AO.
- Detection runs when something looks at the lease. With nobody watching, the restart happens on the first look when a viewer opens the device, so its first tap or two can land during the restart.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Local iOS simulator connections now stay aligned with the simulator’s current boot. When a simulator is restarted outside the app, its connection is refreshed to match.
  * Device lookups now account for simulator boot changes and ignore stale or stopped-device reports.
* **New Features**
  * Simulator listings now include boot information when available, helping the app distinguish between separate simulator sessions.
